turns.response_html:
This is a solid script that successfully implements the logic for finding a specific folder (or creating it if it's missing), iterating through Gmail threads, and saving attachments.

However, there is one logical "gotcha" in your code regarding how you name the files.

The Logic Issue: Execution Date vs. Email Date

Currently, your script uses new Date() to generate the filename:

let today = Utilities.formatDate(new Date(), TIME_ZONE, DATE_FORMAT);

The Problem: This uses the moment the script runs, not the date the email was received.

  • Scenario: You receive a schedule on Friday, but you don't run the script until Monday.
  • Result: The file will be named "2026-01-05 (Monday's date)..." even though the schedule was from Friday. This makes archiving confusing.

The Fix

You should likely use msg.getDate() instead of new Date(). This ensures the filename reflects when the email actually arrived in your inbox.

Here is the revised section of the code with that fix applied:

function saveFarewayExcelsToSubfolder() {
  // --- CONFIGURATION ---
  const PARENT_FOLDER_ID = '1j3aQGl9oZxP-LK5HOGxftMIAV54fJn28';     
  const SUBFOLDER_NAME = 'schedule-excels'; 
  const GMAIL_LABEL = 'Fareway';
  const DATE_FORMAT = "yyyy-MM-dd"; 
  const TIME_ZONE = Session.getScriptTimeZone();
  // ---------------------

  const MS_EXCEL_TYPES = [
    "application/vnd.ms-excel",
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"
  ];

  const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(GMAIL_LABEL);
  if (!label) { Logger.log("Label not found."); return; }
  
  const threads = label.getThreads();
  if (threads.length === 0) { Logger.log("No threads to process."); return; }

  // 1. SETUP FOLDER
  const parentFolder = DriveApp.getFolderById(PARENT_FOLDER_ID);
  let targetFolder;
  const subFolders = parentFolder.getFoldersByName(SUBFOLDER_NAME);
  
  if (subFolders.hasNext()) {
    targetFolder = subFolders.next();
  } else {
    targetFolder = parentFolder.createFolder(SUBFOLDER_NAME);
    Logger.log(`Created new subfolder: ${SUBFOLDER_NAME}`);
  }

  // 2. PROCESS THREADS
  threads.forEach(thread => {
    const messages = thread.getMessages();
    
    messages.forEach(msg => {
      const attachments = msg.getAttachments();
      
      attachments.forEach(attachment => {
        if (MS_EXCEL_TYPES.includes(attachment.getContentType())) {
          try {
            // --- FIX: USE EMAIL DATE, NOT SCRIPT RUN DATE ---
            // We use msg.getDate() here so the file name matches the email timestamp
            let emailDate = Utilities.formatDate(msg.getDate(), TIME_ZONE, DATE_FORMAT);
            let originalName = attachment.getName();
            let newName = `${emailDate} (${originalName})`;

            // Check if file already exists to prevent overwriting or errors
            const existingFiles = targetFolder.getFilesByName(newName);
            if (!existingFiles.hasNext()) {
               let blob = attachment.copyBlob();
               // Create and rename in one step for cleaner logs
               targetFolder.createFile(blob).setName(newName);
               Logger.log(`✅ Saved: ${newName}`);
            } else {
               Logger.log(`⚠️ Skipped (Duplicate): ${newName}`);
            }

          } catch (e) {
            Logger.log(`ERROR processing ${attachment.getName()}: ${e.message}`);
          }
        }
      });
    });

    // 4. REMOVE LABEL (This removes the thread from the queue)
    thread.removeLabel(label);
  });
}

Key Changes Made

  1. Date Source: Changed new Date() to msg.getDate(). This ensures that if you run the script once a month, the files are still named according to the day they were sent.
  2. Duplicate Check: I added a small check (targetFolder.getFilesByName) to see if the file already exists. This prevents the script from creating multiple copies if the label removal fails or if you run the script manually while it's already running.

turns.prompt_text: Can we also add a function that gets all employees who close on Friday night after 8pm, and send me an email showing them?
turns.response_html:
This is a great idea for automation. However, there is a technical hurdle we have to clear first: Google Apps Script cannot read Excel (.xlsx) files directly.

To read the data inside the file, the script must momentarily convert the Excel file into a Google Sheet, read the data, and then (optionally) delete the temporary Google Sheet.

Prerequisite: Enable Drive API

Before using the code below, you must enable the "Drive API" service:

  1. Open your Script Editor.
  2. On the left sidebar, click "Services" (the + button).
  3. Scroll down, select Drive API, and click Add.

The Updated Script

Here is the complete solution. I have updated your main function to call a new helper function (checkFridayClosers) immediately after saving the file.

Note: You may need to adjust the FRIDAY_COL_INDEX and NAME_COL_INDEX variables depending on exactly how your Fareway schedule is formatted.

function saveFarewayExcelsToSubfolder() {
  // --- CONFIGURATION ---
  const PARENT_FOLDER_ID = '1j3aQGl9oZxP-LK5HOGxftMIAV54fJn28';     
  const SUBFOLDER_NAME = 'schedule-excels'; 
  const GMAIL_LABEL = 'Fareway';
  const DATE_FORMAT = "yyyy-MM-dd"; 
  const TIME_ZONE = Session.getScriptTimeZone();
  const YOUR_EMAIL = "your_email@example.com"; // <--- PUT YOUR EMAIL HERE
  // ---------------------

  const MS_EXCEL_TYPES = [
    "application/vnd.ms-excel",
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"
  ];

  const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(GMAIL_LABEL);
  if (!label) { Logger.log("Label not found."); return; }
  
  const threads = label.getThreads();
  if (threads.length === 0) { Logger.log("No threads to process."); return; }

  const parentFolder = DriveApp.getFolderById(PARENT_FOLDER_ID);
  let targetFolder;
  const subFolders = parentFolder.getFoldersByName(SUBFOLDER_NAME);
  
  if (subFolders.hasNext()) { targetFolder = subFolders.next(); } 
  else { targetFolder = parentFolder.createFolder(SUBFOLDER_NAME); }

  threads.forEach(thread => {
    const messages = thread.getMessages();
    messages.forEach(msg => {
      const attachments = msg.getAttachments();
      attachments.forEach(attachment => {
        if (MS_EXCEL_TYPES.includes(attachment.getContentType())) {
          try {
            let emailDate = Utilities.formatDate(msg.getDate(), TIME_ZONE, DATE_FORMAT);
            let originalName = attachment.getName();
            let newName = `${emailDate} (${originalName})`;

            const existingFiles = targetFolder.getFilesByName(newName);
            if (!existingFiles.hasNext()) {
               let blob = attachment.copyBlob();
               let file = targetFolder.createFile(blob).setName(newName);
               Logger.log(`✅ Saved: ${newName}`);

               // --- TRIGGER THE CLOSER CHECK HERE ---
               checkFridayClosers(file.getId(), YOUR_EMAIL);
               // ------------------------------------

            } else {
               Logger.log(`⚠️ Skipped (Duplicate): ${newName}`);
            }
          } catch (e) {
            Logger.log(`ERROR processing ${attachment.getName()}: ${e.message}`);
          }
        }
      });
    });
    thread.removeLabel(label);
  });
}

// --- NEW FUNCTION TO FIND CLOSERS ---
function checkFridayClosers(fileId, emailAddress) {
  try {
    // 1. Convert Excel to temporary Google Sheet to read it
    let excelFile = DriveApp.getFileById(fileId);
    let blob = excelFile.getBlob();
    
    let config = {
      title: "[TEMP] Schedule Parsing",
      parents: [{id: excelFile.getParents().next().getId()}],
      mimeType: MimeType.GOOGLE_SHEETS
    };
    
    // Uses Drive API (Must be enabled in Services)
    let tempFile = Drive.Files.copy(config, fileId); 
    let ss = SpreadsheetApp.openById(tempFile.id);
    let sheet = ss.getSheets()[0]; // Assume first tab
    let data = sheet.getDataRange().getValues();

    // 2. CONFIG: Adjust these based on your specific schedule layout
    // Arrays are zero-indexed. A=0, B=1, C=2, etc.
    const NAME_COL_INDEX = 0; // Column A
    // You might need a loop here to find which column header says "Friday"
    // For now, let's assume Friday is Column F (Index 5)
    const FRIDAY_COL_INDEX = 5; 
    
    let closers = [];

    // 3. Iterate through rows (Skip header row 0)
    for (let i = 1; i < data.length; i++) {
      let row = data[i];
      let name = row[NAME_COL_INDEX];
      let shift = row[FRIDAY_COL_INDEX]; // e.g., "3:00pm - 10:00pm"

      if (isLateShift(shift)) {
        closers.push(`${name} (${shift})`);
      }
    }

    // 4. Send Email if closers found
    if (closers.length > 0) {
      let subject = `Friday Closers: ${excelFile.getName()}`;
      let body = `The following employees are working past 8:00 PM on Friday:\n\n` + closers.join("\n");
      MailApp.sendEmail(emailAddress, subject, body);
      Logger.log(`📧 Email sent to ${emailAddress}`);
    } else {
      Logger.log("No late closers found.");
    }

    // 5. Cleanup: Delete the temp Google Sheet
    DriveApp.getFileById(tempFile.id).setTrashed(true);

  } catch (e) {
    Logger.log(`Error reading schedule: ${e.message}`);
  }
}

// --- HELPER: LOGIC TO CHECK TIME ---
function isLateShift(shiftString) {
  if (!shiftString || typeof shiftString !== 'string') return false;
  
  // Clean up string
  shiftString = shiftString.toLowerCase().trim();

  // Regex to capture the END time. 
  // Looks for patterns like "- 10pm", "- 10:00pm", "- 22:00"
  // This is a simplified regex; schedules vary wildly!
  let match = shiftString.match(/-?\s*(\d{1,2})(:(\d{2}))?\s*(pm|am)?/i);
  
  // If the string is complex, you might need to extract the LAST time mentioned
  // A simple heuristic for grocery schedules: check for specific late hours
  // 8pm, 9pm, 10pm, 11pm (assuming 12hr format)
  
  // Method A: Simple Keyword Check (Easier to maintain)
  if (shiftString.includes("close") || shiftString.includes("cl")) return true;
  
  // Method B: Hour Check
  // If it contains 9pm, 10pm, 11pm
  if (shiftString.includes("9pm") || shiftString.includes("9:00pm")) return true;
  if (shiftString.includes("10pm") || shiftString.includes("10:00pm")) return true;
  if (shiftString.includes("11pm") || shiftString.includes("11:00pm")) return true;
  
  // Handle "8:XX pm" where XX > 00
  if (shiftString.includes("8:15pm") || shiftString.includes("8:30pm")) return true;

  return false;
}

How to customize the isLateShift logic

Schedules are messy. They might say 3-10, 15:00-22:00, or Closing.

The logic I wrote in isLateShift (Method B) is a "Safety Check." It specifically looks for strings containing "9pm", "10pm", or "11pm".

  • If your schedule uses 24hr time (20:00): You will need to change the logic to look for 20:XX, 21:00, etc.
  • If your schedule places the time in a different column: You must update FRIDAY_COL_INDEX (A=0, B=1, C=2, etc.).

That format makes things much easier to parse! Since the data is entered in a shorthand format like "4-10" (Start Hour - End Hour), we can split the text by the dash (-) and look at the second number.

Here is the updated logic. Replace the previous isLateShift function with this new version at the bottom of your script.

Updated Helper Function

This logic looks at the number after the dash. If that number is 9, 10, 11, or 12, it counts as a closer (after 8pm).

// --- HELPER: LOGIC TO CHECK TIME (Updated for "4-10" format) ---
function isLateShift(shiftString) {
  // 1. Safety checks
  if (!shiftString) return false;
  // Convert to string just in case it's read as a number/date
  let str = shiftString.toString().trim(); 
  
  // 2. Split by dash (e.g., "4-10" becomes ["4", "10"])
  let parts = str.split('-');
  
  // If there's no dash, it's not a range we recognize (e.g. "OFF")
  if (parts.length < 2) return false; 

  // 3. Analyze the End Time (the second part)
  // Remove any "pm" or spaces just in case (e.g. "10pm")
  let endString = parts[1].toLowerCase().replace(/[^0-9:]/g, '');
  
  // Handle cases like "10" vs "10:30"
  let timeParts = endString.split(':');
  let hour = parseInt(timeParts[0]);
  let minutes = timeParts.length > 1 ? parseInt(timeParts[1]) : 0;

  // 4. The Rules (Fareway Context)
  // We assume these hours are PM. We want strictly AFTER 8:00 PM.
  
  // Case A: Hour is 9, 10, 11, or 12 -> DEFINITELY LATE
  if (hour >= 9 && hour <= 12) return true;

  // Case B: Hour is 8, but has minutes (e.g., "4-8:15" or "4-8:30")
  if (hour === 8 && minutes > 0) return true;

  return false;
}

⚠️ Critical Step: Verify the "Friday" Column

The script needs to know which column in your Excel file holds the Friday schedule.

  1. Open one of your schedule Excel files.
  2. Count the columns starting from A (A=0, B=1, C=2...).
  3. Update the FRIDAY_COL_INDEX variable in the checkFridayClosers function I gave you previously.

Example: If your Excel looks like this: Name | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat Then Friday is the 6th column, so the index is 5.
